title: Human in the loop: interrupt, resume, time out

concept.heading: Pause the graph before a write, on disk, until a person answers or the clock runs out
paragraphs: LangGraph's interrupt(payload) stops a node and hands the payload to whoever is running the graph: the draft, the tool calls so far, when it was requested. With a checkpointer the paused thread is durable, so the answer can come from another process, hours later, after a restart. Command(resume=value) continues the same node with the decision.

The approval node is where this lives. Approved: it calls create_receipt through the MCP server, which runs its own gate from Module 3 and returns pending_approval. That is not redundancy by accident: the agent's interrupt is the staff member's checkpoint, the server's queue is the director's, and neither layer assumes the other exists. Rejected: nothing is called. Unanswered: expire_pending resumes the thread with a timeout rejection, so a forgotten request never fires a week later when someone clicks.
Timeouts need a clock you can inject, which is why requested_at is recorded in state before the interrupt and the check advances a fake clock.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Start and wait for an approval, with the flow's 30-day timeout and the resume branch. Here you write what the platform did: durable pause, resume with a value, expiry.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: LangGraph interrupt and Command, graph.get_state
pythonBlock.intro: interrupt raises internally and re-runs the node on resume, so everything before it must be idempotent: record requested_at only if unset.

spec: Implement approval_node, pending_interrupt, approve, reject and expire_pending per the stub, and wire approval_node into build_graph.
Run the scripted scenario with an InMemorySaver checkpointer: watch the invoke return with __interrupt__, inspect the payload, approve, and read the server's pending_approval result.
Reject once and confirm no tool was called. Then simulate a forgotten request: advance the clock past the timeout and call expire_pending.
Swap InMemorySaver for a SQLite checkpointer (langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite) if you want the pause to survive a real restart; note what changed.
askClaudeFor: Why interrupt re-executes the node from the top on resume and what that means for side effects before it.
How get_state exposes pending interrupts, so pending_interrupt can be written without guessing.
writeYourself: The decision shape and the reasons you record.

check.command: uv run --directory middleware python checks/run.py m7-2-human-in-loop
check.summary: With a checkpointer the graph pauses before the write and exposes the draft; approve resumes and the write reaches the server's gate as pending_approval; reject never calls a write; an unanswered approval expires after the timeout with the CRM untouched.
